problem:
Find the characteristic equation of the matrix 
$C=[\begin{aligned}4 & 3 & -6 \\ 4 & 5 & -12 \\ 3 & 3 & -7\end{aligned}].$

activity_context.topic_title: The Characteristic Equation of a Matrix

feedback.problem:
$$
C=[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 5 & 0 & 0 \\ -5 & 2 & -3 & 0 \\ 1 & -7 & 6 & 5\end{aligned}].
$$

Consider the matrix $C$ given above. Which of the following statements are true?

- $\lambda =2$ is an eigenvalue of $C$
- $\lambda =5$ is an eigenvalue of $C$
- The eigenvalue $\lambda =5$ has algebraic multiplicity $2$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we find the matrix $\,C-\lambda I:$
﻿﻿﻿

$$
C-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}2-\lambda  & 1 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 5-\lambda  & 0 & 0 \\ -5 & 2 & -3-\lambda  & 0 \\ 1 & -7 & 6 & 5-\lambda \end{aligned}]
$$

The characteristic equation is $det(C-\lambda I)=0.$ 

Notice that we can expand the $4\times 4$ determinant across the $4$th column, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(C-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}2-\lambda  & 1 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 5-\lambda  & 0 & 0 \\ -5 & 2 & -3-\lambda  & 0 \\ 1 & -7 & 6 & 5-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (5-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}2-\lambda  & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 5-\lambda  & 0 \\ -5 & 2 & -3-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Now, expanding the $3\times 3$ determinant across the $2$nd row, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}(5-\lambda )\cdot (5-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}2-\lambda  & 4 \\ -5 & -3-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (5-\lambda )^{2}\cdot ((2-\lambda )(-3-\lambda )+20) & =0 \\ (\lambda -5)^{2}({\lambda }^{2}+\lambda +14) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Since $D<0$ for the polynomial ${\lambda }^{2}+\lambda +14$ we have that the only real eigenvalue is $\lambda =5$ (with algebraic multiplicity $2$). 

Therefore, the correct answer is "II and III only."
